name: Romanian

ancestors.notes: Balkan Romance Vulgar Latin: Eastern Romance branch with no lenition, central vowels, postposed article.

Slavic superstrate (7th c. onwards): massive lexical influence (~40% of vocabulary), some phonological impact (palatalisation patterns, possible influence on central vowels). Old Church Slavonic was the literary/liturgical language until 16th–17th c.
Dacian/Thracian substrate: ~100+ words shared with Albanian of unknown origin (copil, moș, viezure). Possible influence on central vowels /ə, ɨ/ and postposed article.
Greek adstrate: Byzantine influence, shared Balkan sprachbund features.
Turkish adstrate (14th–19th c.): lexical borrowings from Ottoman period.
Hungarian adstrate: centuries of contact in Transylvania. Lexical exchange.

notes: Standard Romanian. Eastern Romance, the ONLY Romance language east of the Adriatic. Key features: (1) Central vowels /ə/ (⟨ă⟩) and /ɨ/ (⟨â/î⟩) — unique in Romance. (2) NO intervocalic lenition (lup, foc — not *lub, *fogo). (3) Postposed definite article (lupul 'the wolf'). (4) Rich diphthong/triphthong system. (5) Rhotacism: intervocalic /l/ → /r/ in some words (soare < SOLEM). (6) Massive Slavic vocabulary layer (~40%). (7) Balkan sprachbund member (Chițoran 2001, Sala 2005). (8) Word-initial ⟨e⟩ is [je] in a closed, cited set: the personal pronouns ⟨eu el ea ei ele⟩ and the present/imperfect forms of ⟨a fi⟩ (⟨e este ești era erai eram erați erau⟩) — everywhere else word-initial ⟨e⟩ is [e] (⟨elev⟩, ⟨examen⟩); this is lexical, so it lives in word_exceptions (DOOM3; Chitoran 2002 ch. 2). (9) ⟨ă⟩ is declared in vowel_graphemes because the engine's closed Latin letter inventory does not carry it; without that declaration every vowel-conditioned rule fails next to it (⟨băieți⟩, ⟨păi⟩). STRESS: Romanian stress is lexical, and the standard spelling does not mark it, but it has a strong default: final stress on a consonant-final word or on a word-final ⟨ea⟩, penultimate stress on any other word (Chițoran 2002: 75-77; Alexei & Ulfsbjorninn 2022: 18). The stress block states that default and its notes list the lexical classes it misses (cópii 'copies' vs copíi 'children' stay unresolved). CEILING: after ⟨c g⟩ a following ⟨i⟩ before a vowel is silent in inherited vocabulary (⟨cioban⟩ [tʃoˈban]) but syllabic in the neologistic layer (⟨Dacia⟩ [ˈdatʃi.a], ⟨sociologie⟩); the split is lexical, not orthographic, so the spec emits the majority syllabic reading and leaves the rest to a caller-supplied lexicon.

stress.notes: Default placement as Chițoran (2002: 75-77) states it, in the tables of Alexei & Ulfsbjorninn (2022: 2-5): a word that ends in a consonant takes final stress (bărbat, animal, magazin), and any other word takes penultimate stress (mare, femeie, mașină). A word that ends in a falling diphthong takes final stress (gunoi, birou, liceu, pârâu; Alexei & Ulfsbjorninn 2022: 18, 21). A word that ends in the diphthong ⟨ea⟩ [e̯a] takes final stress too: "the diphthongs [e̯a] and [o̯a] are only found in stressed position" (Alexei & Ulfsbjorninn 2022: 18), as in stea and curea (2022: 5, Table 2) and acea, stressed ac'ea (Franzén & Horne 1997: 81, (8b)). So cafea, perdea, lalea and the infinitives avea, vedea, putea take the mark on ⟨ea⟩. Word-final ⟨oa⟩ is not an ending here, because no opened source gives a word that ends in it. The default is a tendency, not a law. Chițoran counts the regular class as about one third larger than the lexically marked class (2002: 76, quoted in Alexei & Ulfsbjorninn 2022: 4). A marked word takes penultimate stress when it ends in a consonant (zahăr, călugăr, articol) and antepenultimate stress when it ends in a vowel (pepene, cameră, dragoste). A small set ends in a stressed plain vowel (pane, macara). These words are lexical, and the spec does not list them, so the mark falls one syllable late or early on them. Inflectional endings are outside the stress domain (Franzén & Horne 1997: 75; Alexei & Ulfsbjorninn 2022: 5-6): definite -ul, plural -uri and genitive -lor keep the stress of the stem. The engine reads the ending of the whole word, so lupul, trenuri and caselor take the mark one syllable late. The endings -ei, -ui, -ii and -iu are not final-stress endings: the genitive -ei and -ului and the neologisms in -iu (studiu) are unstressed there. The definite article -a on a noun in -e also writes ⟨ea⟩ (cartea, mintea). It is an inflection outside the stress domain, so the mark falls one syllable late on these forms. Homographs that differ only in stress (módele 'the fashions', modéle 'models'; Franzén & Horne 1997: 75) are not resolved. The ⟨âu⟩ and ⟨ău⟩ entries in ipa_diphthongs keep the falling diphthong in one syllable where the transcription writes it with a syllabic [u].

allophone_rules.notes: ⟨c⟩ is /tʃ/ before ⟨e i⟩; ⟨ch⟩ keeps /k/ (its own grapheme). Chitoran 2002 ch. 2; DOOM3.
⟨g⟩ is /dʒ/ before ⟨e i⟩; ⟨gh⟩ keeps /ɡ/ (its own grapheme). Chitoran 2002 ch. 2; DOOM3.

Word-initial prevocalic /i/ has no onset available and surfaces as the glide [j] — ⟨iarnă⟩ [ˈjarnə], ⟨ied⟩ [jed], ⟨iute⟩ [ˈjute] (Chitoran 2002 ch. 3, glide formation; Vasiliu 1965). A glide needs a nucleus after it and the word needs one at all, so the rule is blocked before another ⟨i⟩ and on a word with no other nucleus: ⟨ii⟩ is [ij], never [jj] (Chitoran 2002 ch. 3; Hayes 2009 ch. 13).

Post-vocalic ⟨i⟩ is the glide [j], falling in a diphthong (⟨mai⟩ [maj], ⟨doi⟩ [doj], ⟨căi⟩ [kəj]) or in the onset of the next syllable (⟨baie⟩ [ˈbaje], ⟨ploaie⟩ [ˈplo̯aje]); the plural+article ⟨-ii⟩ is [ij] (⟨copii⟩ [koˈpij]). Post-consonantal ⟨i⟩ is NOT covered: there it is syllabic and stands in hiatus (⟨Românie⟩ [romɨˈni.e], ⟨abația⟩ [abaˈtsi.a]) — Chitoran 2002 ch. 3. A glide needs a nucleus after it and the word needs one at all, so the rule is blocked before another ⟨i⟩ and on a word with no other nucleus: ⟨ii⟩ is [ij], never [jj] (Chitoran 2002 ch. 3; Hayes 2009 ch. 13).

The word-final desinential ⟨i⟩ (plural, 2sg) is asyllabic: it deletes and palatalizes the preceding consonant — ⟨lupi⟩ [lupʲ], ⟨pomi⟩ [pomʲ], ⟨ochi⟩ [okʲ], ⟨vezi⟩ [vezʲ] (Chitoran 2002 ch. 5, 'final devoiced i'; Renwick 2014; DOOM3). `requires_other_nucleus` keeps the monosyllables that have no other vowel intact — ⟨și⟩ [ʃi], ⟨fi⟩ [fi], ⟨zi⟩ [zi]. Liquids are excluded here and handled by RO_FINAL_I_ASYLLABIC_LIQUID so that the muta cum liquida cluster keeps a syllabic [i].

The same desinence after a liquid, but ONLY where the liquid is not the second member of a muta cum liquida onset: ⟨adevăruri⟩ [adeˈvərurʲ], ⟨fii⟩-type aside. After obstruent+liquid the /i/ must be syllabic because the glide cannot join a complex onset — ⟨noștri⟩ [ˈnoʃtri], ⟨codri⟩ [ˈkodri], ⟨acri⟩ [ˈakri] (Chitoran 2002 ch. 3 and ch. 5, on muta cum liquida; DOOM3).
